patterns: Poland was the weekend's surprise story line: 20 hits (~4.0M) on the Constitutional Tribunal standoff, led by Gunther's 'Hey @Grok, explain what's happening in Poland' (~1.30M at only 0.3% likes), 'Poland's president went in himself' (~431k at 4.6%) and rawsalerts' 'Poland's president cancels trip amid coup allegations' (~292k); the short 'Without X... no one would know what's happening in Poland' post earned 16.6% likes (~216k)

The last-weekend vote push carried the most volume: 120 hits (~5.2M) mention voting or Election Day, with Texas (68 hits, ~3.0M) and Michigan (48 hits, ~2.8M) the two battlegrounds; Michigan posts loved better at 6.5%, led by State Rep. Karen Whitsett crossing over to endorse Mike Rogers (~400k at 13.8%)
Ask-Grok posts buy reach but not love: 11 '@grok' question posts pulled ~2.1M views at a 0.6% like rate (Poland ~1.30M, the daylight-saving clock post ~223k, voter-roll citizenship ~148k)

Obama-legacy posts were the loyal crowd: 14 hits (~1.23M) at 9.2% likes, led by Trump's 'Life Before Obama' checklist (~474k at 11.4%) and Gunther's 'Trump will bury Obama's legacy' call (~300k at 11.4%)

Short, blunt one-liners won on like rate again: 'Dude committed treason.' (~55k at 21.2%), 'Treason.' (~65k at 18.4%) and 'Texas is the red wall. If it falls, we lose.' (~66k at 14.5%), while alx's 'Next stop, Venezuela.' was the top post of the window (~1.59M at 2.4%)

Reach without love: alx's 'Text your friends in Texas' (~371k at 0.4%), rawsalerts' Greenacres aircraft crash (~190k at 0.6%) and Tucker Carlson's Iran nuclear-strike claim (~813k at 1.4%) went wide with few likes; Halloween stories (31 hits, ~1.6M) also ran low at 3.3%, though the 6-year-old in a Border Patrol costume hit 13.2%
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, two searches, about 50 posts) was thin again, with most posts under a few thousand views. The biggest were @kimmonismus on OpenAI reportedly renaming AI as 'superintelligence' and data centers as 'AI compute campuses' (~25k) and @alexgroberman on blocking AI-training crawlers without blocking search crawlers (~24k), then @DailyDarkWeb on attackers posing as ChatGPT and Claude bots to hunt for credentials (~5k). Smaller threads covered OpenAI's deals in the UAE and Samsung executives meeting Sam Altman, OpenAI doubling Pro usage limits, Anthropic's Claude Duet agent and Claude Code refusing to clone games, AI trading accounts at Robinhood, and AI-text watermarks coming to Grok API models. None came close to the watchlist's reach.
narrative_synthesis: A record weekend window: 585 hits and ~31.2M views from 588 originals (Fri ~11:14 ET to Mon ~11:07 ET), just under last weekend's ~31.5M. alx's 'Next stop, Venezuela.' (~1.59M) and Gunther's Poland Grok question (~1.30M) led reach, while the final pre-election push in Texas and Michigan carried the volume and the Obama-legacy and short one-liner posts earned the best like rates. With Election Day tomorrow, the playbook for a creator is simple, practical vote-plan posts tonight, short sincere one-liners, and a calm 'check before you share' angle on fast-moving foreign stories.
